title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 22-24). (X,x) is an n-pointed algebraic curve of type (g,n), first over a field k and then over a subfield K with chosen algebraic closure K̄ embedded in Q̄ (Grothendieck writes Q̃).

The groups involved:
- Π_{X,x} is the geometric profinite fundamental group of the curve X minus its marked points.
- 𝔊_{X,x} is the geometric fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{g,n+1} at the point (X,x,extra point), i.e. the profinite Teichmüller group of type (g,n+1).
- 𝒯_X = 𝔊/Π is the Teichmüller group of type (g,n). The sequence 1→Π→𝔊→𝒯→1 is the profinite Birman exact sequence.
- M_{X,x} is the arithmetic fundamental group π_1(M_{g,n+1} ⊗ Q). It is an extension of Γ_{Q̄/Q} by 𝔊_{X,x}.
- N_{X,x} = M/Π = π_1(M_{g,n} ⊗ Q). It is an extension of Γ_{Q̄/Q} by 𝒯.

On p. 22 Grothendieck built diagram (9) over K. He noted that it reduces to the absolute situation over Q by pulling back the extensions along Γ_{K̄/K} → Γ_{Q̄/Q} (11).

This page records that reduction:
- (12): M_{X,x,K} ≅ M_{X,x} ×_{Γ_Q} Γ_K and N_{X,x,K} ≅ N_{X,x} ×_{Γ_Q} Γ_K.
- (13): the corresponding morphism of extensions, with the same kernel 𝔊_{X,x} and a cartesian right-hand square.
- (13'): the analogue for N, obtained by dividing by Π_{X,x} ⊂ 𝔊_{X,x}. Its kernel is the Teichmüller group 𝒯_{X,x}.

Then the key step. Giving a K-structure on (X,x), i.e. descending the base field of (X,x) from k to K, is equivalent to giving a K-rational point of the moduli stack. Such a point yields a section, up to conjugacy, of M_{X,x,K} → Γ_K. By the cartesian square, this is the same as a lift Γ_K → M_{X,x} over Γ_Q, which is (14) on the next page; similarly (14') for N.

On p. 24 Grothendieck conjectures that this data reconstructs (K, K̄, (X,x)). He then passes to the induced outer action Γ_K → Autext(π_{X,x}).

So the page is an early (1981) formulation of the section/anabelian conjecture for the moduli stacks M_{g,n}, M_{g,n+1}. K-points of moduli are meant to correspond to Galois sections of their arithmetic fundamental groups, and these are linked to the outer Galois representation on the fundamental group of the curve.
errors: The transcription of (13') is internally inconsistent. Dividing by Π_{X,x} ⊂ 𝔊_{X,x} gives kernel 𝒯_{X,x} (the Teichmüller group) in both rows, not π_{X,x} on top and 𝒞_{X,x} below. The image shows a T-like symbol in both places.

Minor point: (12)-(13) silently require a fixed embedding K̄ ⊂ Q̄. The map Γ_K → Γ_Q is injective only if K is algebraic over Q; for K of finite type over Q it is merely a homomorphism. The fibre-product formula still holds.
A section of M_{X,x,K} → Γ_K given by a rational point is defined only up to 𝔊-conjugacy (base-point choice). The page does not yet mention this.

ideas.what: Base change of the arithmetic fundamental-group extension along Γ_K → Γ_Q as a fibre product (cartesian square of extensions)
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of extensions; π_1(Y_K) = π_1(Y) ×_{Γ_Q} Γ_K for Y geometrically connected over Q

ideas.what: Extension of Γ_Q by the profinite Teichmüller group 𝔊 (type g,n+1), with Π ⊂ 𝔊 and quotient the Teichmüller group of type (g,n) (Birman sequence)
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental groups of M_{g,n}; profinite Birman exact sequence
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: K-rational point of moduli (descent of (X,x) to K) gives a section of π_1(M_{g,n+1,K}) → Γ_K, equivalently a lift Γ_K → π_1(M_Q) over Γ_Q, together with the conjecture that this data reconstructs (K, K̄, (X,x))
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture / anabelian conjecture for moduli stacks of curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); later work by Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983), Esquisse d'un programme (moduli M_{g,n} as anabelian)

missed.claim: This is a dated (1981-82) early formulation of the anabelian/section idea for moduli stacks. It predates the 1983 letter to Faltings and is phrased via cartesian squares of extensions over Γ_Q. It documents that the moduli-stack version came together with the curve version in the Teichmüller context.
missed.quote: la donnée de la section x de X_K sur K définissant x sur k (i.e. de la restriction des corps de base de k à K dans (X,x)) s'exprime par une section de l'ext. M_{X,x,K}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it pins down the genesis of the anabelian section philosophy in the Teichmüller-tower notes, before the Faltings letter. The mathematical content itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard: pullback of extensions, and the sections/K-points correspondence for moduli stacks. The anabelian conjecture for M_{g,n} is stated in Grothendieck's 1983 letter and the Esquisse. The only interest is the early dating.
transcription_corrections: First word 'or' (top left) is probably a fragment such as 'par'/'d'où' and not significant.
In (13') the top-left kernel should read 𝒯_{X,x} (Teichmüller group), not π_{X,x}. The bottom-left is also 𝒯_{X,x}, not 𝒞_{X,x}.
In (13') the bottom middle term is N_{X,x,K}, written over a struck M.
In (13') the top right reads Γ_{Q̃/Q} (with 'J' as a stray stroke of Γ), and the bottom right is Γ_{K̄/K}.
'Ceci posé, la donnée de la section x de X_K sur K' is a plausible reading. A struck 'M' precedes X_K.
Last line: 'par une section [com...] de l'ext. M_{X,x,K}'. The superscript 'com' may be part of 'compatible' or 'comme'.
